course_name_original: Técnicas de Expresión Oral y Escrita en Inglés
course_name_en: Oral and Written Expression Techniques in English
prerequisites: Prior knowledge of English grammatical and linguistic structures
Communicative competence at B2 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages

learning_outcomes.text: Follow and give simple oral presentations, making correct use of intonation and expressive possibilities.
Request and offer services related to the work environment, using varied, precise, and appropriate vocabulary for the situation in question.
Participate in meetings and seminars by taking notes, presenting one's own ideas, and making proposals.
Handle routine requests for goods or services over the phone.
Draft and understand formal reports and common professional correspondence in accordance with established rhetorical, grammatical, and lexical norms.

syllabus_topics: Elaboration of technical reports: structure and linguistic characteristics
Participating in socio-professional activities within the company framework
Conducting job interviews and presenting CVs
Participating in debates, meetings, and negotiations
Use of language and linguistic signaling techniques
Use of visual aids and body language
Use of voice: rhythm and emphasis

assessment_methods.method: Partial Exam (E1): Individual written exam on a cover letter
Practical Work (T1): Individual Curriculum Vitae submission
Partial Exam (E2): Individual oral exam on a simulated job interview
Practical Work (T2): Written technical report elaborated jointly by two or more students
Partial Exam (E3): Written exam on the technical report (individual assessment of linguistic and content aspects)
Partial Exam (E4): Group debate participation (individual evaluation)
Partial Exam (E5): Individual oral presentation on a technological innovation topic in engineering
Class Participation (C1): Active participation in practical sessions

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as the sum of E1 + T1 + E2 + T2 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6 + C1. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required to pass the subject. For class participation (C1), students must have a minimum attendance of 80% to practical sessions. For extraordinary calls, students take a theoretical and a practical exam. The final grade is calculated as P1+P2+P3+P4+T1, with a minimum score of 5 out of 10 to pass. Fraudulent use of sources or AI/generative AI and/or partial or total plagiarism in any evaluable activity will result in a 0/10 grade for that activity.
